1.title: Exam Orientation and How to Study
1.text: Welcome to Module zero: Exam Orientation and How to Study. Each part of this module comes from the study notes of the same name, so you can read the notes after you watch.

1.title: What You Will Learn
1.text: By the end of this module you will be able to do five things. The exam at a glance. The five domains. How to answer every question. A study plan. Practice with exam-style questions and a recall check.

1.title: Where This Fits in the Exam
1.text: Here is where this module sits in the exam. Scope: Exam overview, domain map and answer technique (all domains). Exam format: up to ninety questions in ninety minutes; a score of seven hundred twenty on a scale of one hundred to nine hundred passes. Validated against: the official Comp T I A Network plus N ten to nine exam objectives, version four point zero.

1.title: The exam at a glance
1.text: The exam at a glance. Exam code. N ten to nine (version nine). Questions. A maximum of ninety. Question types. Multiple-choice and performance-based (simulations). Time. ninety minutes. Passing score. seven hundred twenty on a scale of one hundred to nine hundred. Recommended experience. nine to twelve months in the I T networking field. Lifecycle. Launched June twenty, two thousand twenty-four; Comp T I A exams usually retire about three years after launch (estimated two thousand twenty-seven). Exam tip: Performance-based questions come first. They are simulations (drag and drop, configure a device, read a diagram). They take longer, so flag them and return if you are short of time, but do not skip them.

1.title: The five domains
1.text: The five domains. The figure shows this: Domain map: five domains, twenty-five objectives and the modules that cover them.

1.title: The five domains, continued
1.text: The five domains. one point zero Networking Concepts. Weight: twenty-three percent. Objectives: one point one to one point eight. two point zero Network Implementation. Weight: twenty percent. Objectives: two point one to two point four. three point zero Network Operations. Weight: nineteen percent. Objectives: three point one to three point five. four point zero Network Security. Weight: fourteen percent. Objectives: four point one to four point three. five point zero Network Troubleshooting. Weight: twenty-four percent. Objectives: five point one to five point five. Exam tip: Troubleshooting (twenty-four percent) and concepts (twenty-three percent) together are almost half the exam. Learn the troubleshooting method and the ports, protocols and subnetting cold.

1.title: How to answer every question
1.text: How to answer every question. Read the last line to see what is asked. Identify the O S I layer or the device the scenario points to. Eliminate options that belong to a different layer or a different protocol. Choose the simplest explanation that fits all the facts. Answer every question; never leave a blank. Comp T I A lists acronyms the exam may use; this course spells every acronym out the first time.

1.title: A study plan
1.text: A study plan. one. Modules: one to seven. Goal: Concepts: O S I, appliances, cloud, ports, media, subnetting. two. Modules: eight to eleven. Goal: Implementation: routing, switching, wireless, racks. three. Modules: twelve to sixteen. Goal: Operations: documentation, monitoring, D R, services, access. four. Modules: seventeen to nineteen. Goal: Security. five. Modules: twenty to twenty-five. Goal: Troubleshooting and final practice.

1.title: Practice Question 1
1.text: Question one. What is the passing score for the N ten to nine exam? The four options are on the screen. The answer is B: seven hundred twenty on a scale of one hundred to nine hundred. The passing score is seven hundred twenty on a scale of one hundred to nine hundred.

1.title: Practice Question 2
1.text: Question two. A candidate meets a long simulation question at the start of the exam. What is the best approach? The four options are on the screen. The answer is B: Flag it, answer the quicker questions, and return to the simulation. Performance-based questions are scored, but taking them later saves time for the rest.

1.title: Practice Question 3
1.text: Question three. Which two domains together carry the largest share of the exam? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C: Network Troubleshooting and Networking Concepts. Troubleshooting (twenty-four percent) and concepts (twenty-three percent) are the two largest.

1.title: Practice Question 4
1.text: Question four. How many questions can the exam contain at most? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C: ninety. The exam has a maximum of ninety questions.

1.title: Recall Check 1
1.text: Recall check one. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question one. What is the exam code? Answer: N ten to nine. Question two. How long is the exam? Answer: ninety minutes. Question three. Name the two question types. Answer: Multiple-choice and performance-based.

1.title: Recall Check 2
1.text: Recall check two. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question four. Which domain has the highest weight? Answer: Network Troubleshooting, at twenty-four percent. Question five. What is the lowest domain weight? Answer: Network Security, at fourteen percent. Question six. How much networking experience does Comp T I A recommend? Answer: nine to twelve months.

1.title: Module Recap
1.text: Here is the recap. Format: up to ninety questions, ninety minutes, seven hundred twenty of nine hundred, multiple-choice and performance-based. Weights: twenty-three or twenty or nineteen or fourteen or twenty-four percent. Method: find the layer or device, eliminate, pick the simplest fit. Simulations: flag and return; never skip. If this course is helping you, please subscribe to the channel and hit the bell icon, so you get a notification when the next video is out. In the next module, we continue the course.
